activations.domainDescription: Executive clinical reasoning and treatment planning
activations.domainFunction: Synthesizes patient data, evidence, and clinical judgment into diagnostic and treatment decisions
activations.whyThisNode: dlPFC is the executive planner — clinical decision-making requires the same working memory, planning, and judgment functions

treatments.label: Structured diagnostic checklist
treatments.description: Implement standardized differential diagnosis checklists to reduce cognitive bias and oversight errors

treatments.label: Clinical decision audit
treatments.description: Retrospective case review of diagnostic accuracy and treatment outcome correlation across provider caseload

activations.domainDescription: Emotional attunement and rapport with patients
activations.domainFunction: Builds and maintains the therapeutic relationship that predicts treatment outcomes across all modalities
activations.whyThisNode: vmPFC mediates emotional valuation and social bonding — the neural substrate of the empathic connection that defines therapeutic alliance

treatments.label: Alliance repair protocol
treatments.description: Structured rupture-repair interventions when therapeutic relationship strain is detected via outcome measures

treatments.label: Patient satisfaction tracking
treatments.description: Session-by-session outcome rating scale (ORS) and session rating scale (SRS) to monitor alliance quality

activations.domainDescription: Rapid clinical pattern detection and gut-level diagnostic sensing
activations.domainFunction: Detects subtle patient presentation patterns that trigger diagnostic hypotheses before conscious analysis completes
activations.whyThisNode: Anterior insula drives interoceptive awareness and gut-feeling — experienced clinicians use somatic markers for rapid pattern recognition

treatments.label: Clinical supervision for pattern calibration
treatments.description: Regular peer supervision focused on reviewing intuitive diagnostic hunches against outcome data

treatments.label: Diagnostic accuracy tracking
treatments.description: Track initial diagnostic impressions against final diagnoses to calibrate clinical intuition over time

activations.domainDescription: Detection of clinical errors, near-misses, and deviations from standard of care
activations.domainFunction: Monitors for discrepancies between intended and actual clinical performance, flagging errors before harm occurs
activations.whyThisNode: dACC is the brain's error detector — quality control in provider systems requires the same conflict monitoring function

treatments.label: Near-miss reporting system
treatments.description: Implement no-blame near-miss reporting to capture errors before they reach patients

treatments.label: Morbidity and mortality review
treatments.description: Regular case conferences reviewing adverse outcomes and diagnostic errors for system-level learning

activations.domainDescription: Provider emotional resonance with patient suffering
activations.domainFunction: Enables the provider to feel and understand patient distress without being overwhelmed by it
activations.whyThisNode: Empathy network activation is the neural basis of compassionate care — and its chronic activation drives burnout

treatments.label: Compassion fatigue prevention program
treatments.description: Structured self-care, peer support, and caseload management to sustain empathic capacity

treatments.label: Burnout screening (MBI)
treatments.description: Quarterly Maslach Burnout Inventory screening for emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment

activations.domainDescription: Stored medical knowledge, case histories, and evidence base
activations.domainFunction: Encodes and retrieves the clinical knowledge, training, and case experience that informs diagnostic reasoning
activations.whyThisNode: Hippocampus is the memory system — clinical expertise depends on vast stored pattern libraries of cases and evidence

treatments.label: Continuing education protocol
treatments.description: Structured CME/CEU program targeting identified knowledge gaps in diagnostic accuracy

treatments.label: Knowledge currency audit
treatments.description: Assess provider familiarity with current evidence-based guidelines versus outdated practices

activations.domainDescription: Routing patient information to appropriate clinical resources
activations.domainFunction: Triages incoming clinical information and routes it to the appropriate specialist, team, or level of care
activations.whyThisNode: Thalamus is the brain's relay center — intake triage performs the same routing function for clinical information flow

treatments.label: Triage protocol standardization
treatments.description: Implement validated triage tools (PHQ-9, Columbia Protocol) at intake to standardize routing decisions

treatments.label: Routing accuracy review
treatments.description: Track percentage of patients routed to correct level of care at first contact versus requiring re-routing

activations.domainDescription: Provider verbal communication, documentation, and reporting
activations.domainFunction: Generates clinical notes, treatment plans, referral letters, and verbal communication with patients and colleagues
activations.whyThisNode: Broca's area drives speech production — clinical communication is the output channel for all provider intelligence

treatments.label: Standardized handoff protocol (SBAR)
treatments.description: Implement Situation-Background-Assessment-Recommendation format for all clinical handoffs

treatments.label: Communication failure audit
treatments.description: Review adverse events for communication root causes — missed handoffs, unclear documentation, lost referrals

activations.domainDescription: Understanding patient narratives, research, and clinical data
activations.domainFunction: Processes and comprehends incoming clinical language — patient history, lab results, research literature
activations.whyThisNode: Wernicke's area drives language comprehension — understanding patient stories and clinical data is the input channel

treatments.label: Active listening training
treatments.description: Motivational interviewing and reflective listening training to improve patient narrative comprehension

treatments.label: Clinical literacy assessment
treatments.description: Evaluate provider comfort with current evidence base, statistical literacy, and research interpretation

activations.domainDescription: Adherence to clinical standards, ethics, and legal requirements
activations.domainFunction: Inhibits clinical shortcuts and enforces adherence to standard of care, ethics codes, and regulatory requirements
activations.whyThisNode: vlPFC is the brain's inhibitory control center — compliance requires suppressing expedient shortcuts in favor of proper procedure

treatments.label: Compliance training refresh
treatments.description: Annual mandatory training on HIPAA, informed consent, duty to warn, and scope of practice boundaries

treatments.label: Compliance audit
treatments.description: Chart review for documentation completeness, consent forms, and adherence to clinical protocols

activations.domainDescription: Interpersonal bonding and trust within clinical teams
activations.domainFunction: Builds the trust, psychological safety, and cohesion that enable effective multidisciplinary clinical teamwork
activations.whyThisNode: Oxytocin drives social bonding and trust — clinical team function depends on the same bonding neurobiology

treatments.label: Team-based care implementation
treatments.description: Structured interdisciplinary team meetings, shared case conceptualization, and collaborative treatment planning

treatments.label: Team climate survey
treatments.description: Anonymous team psychological safety survey to identify trust deficits and interpersonal friction points

activations.domainDescription: Chronic stress activation in provider systems
activations.domainFunction: Tracks and responds to systemic stress — caseload pressure, administrative burden, and vicarious trauma
activations.whyThisNode: HPA axis is the stress response system — provider burnout is a chronic HPA activation syndrome driven by unrelenting clinical demand

treatments.label: Caseload management protocol
treatments.description: Set evidence-based caseload caps with acuity weighting — high-acuity cases count as 1.5-2x standard

treatments.label: Provider stress biomarker tracking
treatments.description: Track sick days, turnover intention, and self-reported stress to detect system-level burnout before crisis

activations.domainDescription: Clinical risk evaluation and threat detection
activations.domainFunction: Evaluates patient risk — suicidality, violence, deterioration — and triggers appropriate crisis protocols
activations.whyThisNode: Amygdala drives threat detection — clinical risk assessment is the provider analog of rapid threat evaluation

treatments.label: Standardized risk assessment protocol
treatments.description: Implement Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale and violence risk instruments at every intake and crisis contact

treatments.label: Risk assessment calibration
treatments.description: Review outcomes of risk assessments to calibrate provider sensitivity and specificity for true positives

activations.domainDescription: Automatic crisis intervention activation
activations.domainFunction: Triggers immediate crisis response protocols — safety planning, hospitalization, emergency contacts — when risk thresholds are exceeded
activations.whyThisNode: Central amygdala triggers automatic defensive responses — crisis protocols activate automatically when clinical risk is detected

treatments.label: Crisis protocol drill schedule
treatments.description: Quarterly crisis response drills including active suicidality, medical emergency, and violence threat scenarios

treatments.label: Crisis response time audit
treatments.description: Track time from crisis detection to intervention initiation across all crisis events

activations.domainDescription: Executive oversight and coordination of multidisciplinary care
activations.domainFunction: Coordinates treatment across providers, specialties, and levels of care — the executive function of the clinical system
activations.whyThisNode: Frontoparietal network coordinates complex executive function — clinical coordination requires the same multi-component orchestration

treatments.label: Care coordination protocol
treatments.description: Designated care coordinator role with shared treatment plan across all providers on each case

treatments.label: Fragmentation index tracking
treatments.description: Measure number of providers per patient, handoff failures, and contradictory treatment plans

activations.domainDescription: Ongoing professional development and evidence integration
activations.domainFunction: Processes new clinical evidence, integrates training, and updates provider competency through language-based learning
activations.whyThisNode: Language network underpins all clinical learning — reading research, attending lectures, and processing new evidence-based guidelines

treatments.label: Evidence-based practice training
treatments.description: Monthly journal club and case conference focused on integrating current research into clinical practice

treatments.label: Practice pattern analysis
treatments.description: Compare individual provider treatment patterns against evidence-based guidelines to identify drift

activations.domainDescription: Understanding patient subjective experience and worldview
activations.domainFunction: Enables provider to take the patient's perspective — understanding their lived experience, values, and treatment preferences
activations.whyThisNode: TPJ mediates theory of mind and perspective-taking — the neural basis of understanding another person's subjective reality

treatments.label: Cultural competency training
treatments.description: Ongoing training in cultural humility, health literacy accommodation, and shared decision-making

treatments.label: Patient experience survey
treatments.description: Systematic patient feedback on feeling heard, understood, and respected by their provider

activations.domainDescription: Baseline emotional tone and morale of the provider system
activations.domainFunction: Maintains the serotonergic tone of the clinical system — the baseline mood, satisfaction, and sense of purpose
activations.whyThisNode: Raphe serotonin sets baseline mood — organizational morale is the system-level analog of serotonergic tone

treatments.label: Meaning and purpose cultivation
treatments.description: Regular reconnection with clinical mission through patient outcome stories and impact recognition

treatments.label: Organizational climate survey
treatments.description: Annual provider satisfaction and engagement survey tracking morale, autonomy, and purpose over time

activations.domainDescription: Standard operating procedures and clinical routines
activations.domainFunction: Executes the habitual clinical workflows — intake procedures, session structure, documentation routines — that keep the system running
activations.whyThisNode: Striatum drives habit and routine — clinical workflows are the procedural habits that enable consistent care delivery

treatments.label: Workflow optimization review
treatments.description: Map clinical workflows end-to-end and eliminate unnecessary administrative burden that drives burnout

treatments.label: Administrative burden measurement
treatments.description: Track provider time allocation — direct clinical versus documentation versus administrative tasks

activations.domainDescription: Maintaining consistent care across time and transitions
activations.domainFunction: Ensures patient care continuity across provider changes, level-of-care transitions, and treatment phases
activations.whyThisNode: Cingulo-opercular network maintains sustained task sets — continuity of care requires the same persistent monitoring across time

treatments.label: Warm handoff protocol
treatments.description: Three-way session with outgoing provider, incoming provider, and patient for every care transition

treatments.label: Continuity gap analysis
treatments.description: Track patients lost to follow-up, missed transitions, and care gaps across the provider network

issues.label: Provider Burnout / Compassion Fatigue
issues.summary: Chronic depletion of provider emotional resources leading to depersonalization, cynicism, and reduced clinical effectiveness

circuits.detail: Provider stress response system chronically elevated — caseload exceeds sustainable capacity
Empathic capacity exhausted — provider emotionally numb to patient suffering, going through motions
Therapeutic alliance quality degraded — provider unable to form genuine emotional connection with patients
Clinical decision-making quality declining — cognitive fatigue reduces diagnostic accuracy
System morale collapsed — pervasive cynicism, loss of professional meaning and purpose
Team cohesion eroded — interpersonal trust and collaboration replaced by isolation and self-protection

issues.label: Diagnostic Error / Missed Diagnosis
issues.summary: Failure to correctly identify patient conditions due to cognitive bias, knowledge gaps, or system failures

circuits.detail: Clinical reasoning compromised by anchoring bias, premature closure, or availability heuristic
Clinical intuition generating false pattern matches — high confidence in incorrect diagnostic impressions
Clinical knowledge base not updated — provider relying on obsolete diagnostic criteria or treatment evidence
Error monitoring suppressed by time pressure — quality control shortcuts under high-volume demands
Patient narrative incompletely processed — key diagnostic clues in history missed or dismissed

issues.label: Care Fragmentation
issues.summary: Patient care split across disconnected providers with poor coordination, conflicting plans, and lost transitions

circuits.detail: Clinical coordination absent — multiple providers operating independently without shared treatment plan
Continuity of care disrupted at every transition — patients falling through gaps between providers
Information routing failures — referrals lost, reports unsent, critical data not reaching treating providers
Clinical communication siloed — providers documenting in separate systems without cross-access
Clinical workflows lack standardization across providers — different protocols create contradictory care
Compliance standards not enforced across network — each provider operating by their own rules

issues.label: Crisis System Overflow
issues.summary: Volume of acute clinical crises exceeds system capacity, leading to delayed response and patient harm

circuits.detail: Crisis protocols saturated — too many simultaneous emergencies for standard response capacity
Risk assessment generating constant high-priority alerts — everything flagged as critical, nothing triaged effectively
Intake triage backed up — patients waiting hours or days for crisis-level assessment
Provider stress at maximum — crisis team burning out from sustained emergency-level operations
Clinical coordination overwhelmed — unable to track all active crisis cases simultaneously

issues.label: Treatment Resistance
issues.summary: Standard interventions failing to produce expected outcomes despite appropriate diagnosis and protocol adherence

circuits.detail: Clinical decision-making exhausted conventional options — standard algorithms completed without improvement
Knowledge base lacks alternatives — provider uncertain what to try next beyond standard-of-care options
Treatment plan not adequately integrated across specialties — individual providers optimizing in isolation
Patient perspective not adequately incorporated — treatment imposed rather than collaboratively designed
Treatment continuity broken — gains from one provider undermined by gaps or contradictions from another

issues.label: Clinical Communication Breakdown
issues.summary: Failures in provider-patient or provider-provider communication leading to errors, mistrust, and poor outcomes

circuits.detail: Clinical output garbled — documentation incomplete, verbal handoffs missing critical information
Comprehension failures — patient concerns misunderstood, clinical data misinterpreted between providers
Therapeutic alliance ruptured — patient feels unheard, misunderstood, or dismissed by provider
Empathic attunement lost — provider communicating technical information without emotional resonance
Perspective-taking absent — provider failing to adapt communication to patient health literacy and culture
